text:
How long does it take to get a passport once biometrics are done?
Fourteen (14) days as stipulated in the service charter.
heading: How long does it take to get a passport once biometrics are done?

text:
What happens if my date of birth or name differs between my ID and birth certificate?
Make the necessary correction by visiting either Civil Registration Services or the National Registration Bureau (NRB) before applying. The primary documents — birth certificate and national ID — must contain the same information.
heading: What happens if my date of birth or name differs between my ID and birth certificate?

text:
What happens if I discover I do not have all requirements on my appointment date?
You can reschedule the appointment to the next available date, or visit the customer care desk at your passport application centre for facilitation on submission and biometrics capture.
heading: What happens if I discover I do not have all requirements on my appointment date?

text:
Why must I bring physical documents when I already uploaded everything?
A passport is a security document; physical documents are required for multiple storage of record.
heading: Why must I bring physical documents when I already uploaded everything?

text:
Can someone else bring a child for biometrics?
Due to child protection laws, the biological parent must apply and present the child for biometrics, unless one has legal guardianship from the courts.
heading: Can someone else bring a child for biometrics?

text:
What is a consent form?
Authorization by the biological parent or legal guardian to the Directorate for a passport to be issued to a minor.
heading: What is a consent form?

text:
Can I renew or replace my passport outside the country?
Yes, through consular services at Kenya High Commissions and Embassies.
heading: Can I renew or replace my passport outside the country?

text:
How do I track the progress of my passport?
Log in to your eCitizen account, or SMS your application number (on your receipt) to 22222.
heading: How do I track the progress of my passport?

text:
Do I need a certified recommender's ID copy?
A recommender's ID copy is no longer a requirement.
heading: Do I need a certified recommender's ID copy?

text:
Can I collect my passport from a different centre than where I applied?
No. A passport is collected from the passport centre where you did your biometrics.
heading: Can I collect my passport from a different centre than where I applied?

text:
What do I need to collect my passport when it is ready?
Carry the invoice with a token attached and your original national ID. For a replacement, also bring the old passport booklet.
heading: What do I need to collect my passport when it is ready?

text:
Outdated or wrong passport fee figures you may see (KES 4,550, 6,050, 12,050)
KES 4,550 is the pre-March-2024 price of the 34-page passport. It still appears on a stale official legacy eCitizen help page and on Wikipedia, but budgeting on it leads to underpayment — the current 34-page price is KES 7,550. KES 6,050 and KES 7,550 were the pre-2024 prices of the 50-page and 66-page booklets respectively. KES 12,050 for the 66-page booklet is an error that appears in aggregator guides and even on a stale DIS fees page — the gazetted base is KES 12,500, so the payable eCitizen figure is KES 12,550 (12,050 was actually the pre-2024 lost-passport replacement fee, which likely seeded the mix-up). The separate cheap "East African passport" (KES 990) no longer exists as a category. If a price you have seen disagrees with the eCitizen payment step, trust the payment step.
heading: Outdated or wrong passport fee figures you may see (KES 4,550, 6,050, 12,050)
source: resolved fee research — Kenya Gazette Notice 15493 (14 Nov 2023), Kenya High Commission London fee table, DIS statements and 2026 reporting

text:
Why passport prices seem to disagree — booklet sizes and availability changes
Passport prices differ by booklet size (34, 50, or 66 pages), and the booklet menu on eCitizen has changed several times: the 34-page was withdrawn in July 2025, the 50-page was removed around February 2026 (briefly leaving only the 66-page at KES 12,550 as the cheapest option), and the 34-page returned around June 2026 as the only selectable option. The gazetted prices themselves have not changed since 1 March 2024. This availability churn — plus stale official pages still showing pre-2024 prices — is why different sources quote different prices for "a passport".
heading: Why passport prices seem to disagree — booklet sizes and availability changes
source: resolved fee research — Kenya Gazette Notice 15493 (14 Nov 2023), Kenya High Commission London fee table, DIS statements and 2026 reporting

text:
Passport fees — how much a passport costs and how to pay
The standard first passport (34-page A Series ordinary) costs KES 7,550 on eCitizen (gazetted KES 7,500 plus the KES 50 eCitizen convenience fee; Kenya Gazette Notice 15493 of November 2023, in force since 1 March 2024). Larger booklets: 50-page B Series KES 9,550; 66-page C Series KES 12,550. Replacement of a lost or mutilated passport: KES 20,050. Booklet availability on eCitizen has fluctuated throughout the 2025–26 booklet shortage — at times only one booklet size has been selectable — so the fee shown at the eCitizen payment step is the authoritative price. Payment is via M-Pesa, Airtel Money, debit/credit card, or online banking through the eCitizen gateway. Two payment invoices are issued after paying — download and print both before closing the tab.
heading: Passport fees — how much a passport costs and how to pay
source: Njia knowledge pack — verified against Kenya Gazette Notice 15493 (14 Nov 2023), DIS pages (archived Feb–May 2026), Kenya High Commission London, DIS Service Delivery Charter 2025

text:
Processing timelines — how long it takes to get the passport
Official timelines differ slightly between government sources: the eCitizen portal quotes 10 working days for first-time applications, the DIS Service Delivery Charter says 14 working days, and the DIS FAQ says fourteen (14) days from biometric capture — plan for roughly two to three weeks. A gazetted Express Passport tier exists — 34-page booklet at KES 30,000 (Kenya Gazette Notice 15493 of November 2023). In practice, urgent cases with documentary proof (medical emergency, studies, or a job abroad) are handled at a dedicated desk at Nyayo House, Nairobi; in March 2026 the government announced a 72-hour channel for applicants with jobs abroad. Diaspora applications through High Commissions and Embassies take longer, roughly 4–8 weeks.
heading: Processing timelines — how long it takes to get the passport
source: Njia knowledge pack — verified against Kenya Gazette Notice 15493 (14 Nov 2023), DIS pages (archived Feb–May 2026), Kenya High Commission London, DIS Service Delivery Charter 2025

text:
Processing centres — where to book your appointment
There are ten passport processing centres where you can book your biometrics appointment: Nairobi (Nyayo House), Kisumu, Mombasa, Eldoret, Nakuru, Embu, Kisii, Kericho, Bungoma, and Garissa (opened February 2025). You may book any centre through eCitizen — pick the most convenient. The passport is collected at the same centre where your biometrics were taken. Applicants near Thika typically book Nairobi (Nyayo House), about 40 km away; if Nyayo House appointment slots are congested, Embu (about 90 km) is the nearest alternative. Diaspora applicants use the nearest Kenya High Commission or Embassy.
heading: Processing centres — where to book your appointment
source: Njia knowledge pack — verified against Kenya Gazette Notice 15493 (14 Nov 2023), DIS pages (archived Feb–May 2026), Kenya High Commission London, DIS Service Delivery Charter 2025

text:
Documents to bring to the appointment — first-time adult applicant
Bring to your biometrics appointment: original birth certificate and a copy; original national ID and a copy; the printed eCitizen application form (Form 19) and both payment invoices. You do not need printed passport photos — your photo is captured live at the biometrics appointment (the online form may ask for a digital photo upload, and diaspora applicants at embassies may still need printed photos). Warning: a name or date-of-birth mismatch between your national ID and birth certificate causes rejection — correct the birth certificate at Civil Registration Services or the ID at the National Registration Bureau before applying. Minors need extra documents including parental consent.
heading: Documents to bring to the appointment — first-time adult applicant
source: Njia knowledge pack — verified against Kenya Gazette Notice 15493 (14 Nov 2023), DIS pages (archived Feb–May 2026), Kenya High Commission London, DIS Service Delivery Charter 2025

text:
Application flow — the steps from start to finish
Register or log in on eCitizen at dis.ecitizen.go.ke, open Directorate of Immigration Services, choose New Applications, complete Form 19 online and upload the required documents, pay the fee, download and print the two payment invoices, book an appointment at one of the ten processing centres, attend in person for biometric capture (photo and fingerprints), and collect the passport from that same centre once notified (carry your invoice and original national ID). The Recommending Officer section of Form 19 is optional since July 2026 — an application is no longer held up for lack of a recommender.
heading: Application flow — the steps from start to finish
source: Njia knowledge pack — verified against Kenya Gazette Notice 15493 (14 Nov 2023), DIS pages (archived Feb–May 2026), Kenya High Commission London, DIS Service Delivery Charter 2025

text:
Kenya Passport and Travel Documents (official DIS page)
The Government of Kenya issues ePassports to citizens, valid for 10 years, in compliance with ICAO document 9303 and the East African Community Summit resolution.

Passport applicants apply online and pay requisite fees through the eCitizen portal at dis.ecitizen.go.ke. The various categories of Kenya passports and applicable fees are described on the DIS fees page.

Upon completing the application and paying applicable fees, applicants must book an appointment through the eCitizen portal and select one of the Passport Processing Centres to submit applications and enrol biometrics (photo capture / biometric): Nairobi (Nyayo House), Kisumu, Mombasa, Eldoret, Nakuru, Embu, Kisii, Kericho and Bungoma — plus Garissa, opened February 2025, which the static DIS page predates (ten centres in total).

Kenyan Diaspora in need of passport services may contact the nearest Kenya High Commission or Embassy for appointments and further assistance.
heading: Kenya Passport and Travel Documents (official DIS page)
source: https://immigration.go.ke/passport-section/ (archived 2026-04-11; Garissa note added from official DIS announcements)
